title: Zariski's Main Theorem for a monogenic algebra
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $I\subseteq R[X]$ an ideal of the polynomial ring [def-weil-polynomial-ring] and $S=R[X]/I$, an $R$-algebra of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Let $\mathfrak q\subset S$ be a prime ideal such that $R\to S$ is quasi-finite at $\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime], and let $S'\subseteq S$ be the integral closure of $R$ in $S$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Then there is $g\in S'$ with $g\notin\mathfrak q$ such that the map $S'_g\to S_g$, $y/g^n\mapsto y/g^n$, of localizations at the powers of $g$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away] induced by the inclusion $S'\subseteq S$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00Q8 (lemma-quasi-finite-monogenic, line 30735; its proof uses Lemma 00PQ)

proof.text: Set S = Polynomial R / I and p = q.comap (algebraMap R S). The finite-type instance for S is provided by Mathlib for a polynomial quotient. Unfold IsQuasiFiniteAtPrime: its hypothesis is openness of the singleton of e(q), where e = PrimeSpectrum.preimageHomeomorphFiber R S p. Using e.isOpen_image and Set.image_singleton, transport this openness back to the singleton of q in the topological fibre comap(algebraMap R S)^{-1}{p}. The fibre homeomorphism is the proved Mathlib declaration used directly, not the project fibre-bijection theorem.

Apply the proved Mathlib theorem Algebra.QuasiFiniteAt.of_isOpen_singleton_fiber to that open singleton. This gives Algebra.QuasiFiniteAt R q.asIdeal; register it as a local instance. This explicitly bridges the project isolated-point definition and Mathlib quasi-finiteness, rather than identifying them by fiat.

Apply the proved Mathlib theorem Algebra.ZariskisMainProperty.of_finiteType (Stacks Tag 00Q9) to q.asIdeal. Its conclusion unfolds by definition to an element g of integralClosure R S outside q and bijectivity of Localization.awayMap of the canonical inclusion, exactly the unchanged conclusion. This uses the public finite-type theorem, not the private monogenic theorem.
